hypotheses.reasoning: At 22:04:17 session-cache was restarted after a node replacement with no RDB snapshot, so it came back with 0 keys (#2828). account-svc then saw a 93% miss ratio against a 6% baseline and sent every lookup to accounts-db (#2887). That cache stampede filled accounts-db: 490 of 500 connections in use with CPU at 98–99% (#2921, #3016). After that, account-svc queries on accounts timed out at 5s (#3045 onward), and edge-proxy returned 504s on POST /login starting at 22:06. The trigger, a cold cache, would have been survivable alone. The outage came from the load amplification. Other things in the window don't fit: the template-svc/mailer circuit, the legacy-inventory healthcheck, metrics-agent drops, the disk warning, the TLS cert warning and a single audit_log slow query are all unrelated noise.
Another reading is that accounts-db queries simply time out. But the database overload is explained by the stampede after the cache cold start.
accounts-db hit its connection and CPU limits, but only because of the abnormal miss load, not ordinary traffic.

verdict.recommendedAction: Shed or rate-limit login traffic and add request coalescing (single-flight) for cache misses in account-svc so accounts-db can recover. Warm session-cache from accounts-db at a controlled rate. Enable RDB/AOF persistence, or a warm-up step, for session-cache node replacements, and add jittered backoff to cache-miss loads.
